Issue Reading note
One segment; product-line ARR is transcript-only Cloud Security, Next-Gen Identity and Next-Gen SIEM ARR, gross retention and module adoption appear only in earnings calls, releases and investor briefings, as rounded "more than" minimums. The core-platform figures used throughout are residuals (total ARR less the three minimums) and are therefore maximums. Management re-bases these series: Falcon Shield moved from Cloud into Identity in Q2 FY2026, the 5-or-more-module metric was retired after Q4 FY2025, and the subscription-customer count stopped at 29,000 for FY2024 against "more than 88,000 organizations" in the FY2026 10-K on a basis that includes MSSP end customers.
The July 19, 2024 incident distorts FY2025 and FY2026 Customer commitment packages worth about $80m of ARR value, a related partner programme and $177.8m of incident costs net of insurance over two years separated ARR from revenue by a guided $10-15m a quarter through FY2026 and depressed net new ARR, retention and expense lines. The DOJ and SEC have requested information on revenue recognition and ARR reporting for certain customers, and that request is open.
FY2027 margin comparisons are flattered Lengthening commission amortisation from four to five years adds $85-95m to FY2027 non-GAAP operating income ($53.4m realised in H1), and FY2027 laps $44.8m of Strategic Plan restructuring and most of $117.7m of FY2026 incident costs. Every FY2027 margin figure below names its basis.
GAAP and non-GAAP diverge by more than a fifth of revenue FY2026 GAAP loss from operations was $(293.3)m against non-GAAP operating income of $1,046m; H1 FY2027 stock compensation was $674.6m, 23.6% of revenue. Consensus FY2029 GAAP EPS of $0.547 is 27% of the non-GAAP $2.058.

1. Business description, model and unit economics

CrowdStrike sells cybersecurity software as a subscription. One agent, the Falcon sensor, is installed on a customer's laptops, servers, virtual machines, containers and domain controllers; it streams filtered telemetry to CrowdStrike's cloud, blocks attacks locally, and keeps working offline. Thirty-three cloud modules run on that one agent, and a customer buys more of them over time without deploying anything new▪: "it's every customer's next-gen SIEM enabled. Like the data is just in the platform. So it's just a matter of signing up and paying for the license entitlement" (Q2 FY2027 call). Subscriptions run one to three years, are non-cancelable, and are invoiced upfront or in instalments. The vast majority of sales flow through resellers, distributors, managed security service providers and cloud marketplaces (FY2026 10-K, Partnership Ecosystem).

The company reports one operating segment. Revenue is disaggregated two ways only:

1.1 Core Falcon platform: endpoint, managed detection, exposure management, services

About 63% of ending ARR at July 2026 and about 68% of revenue once professional services is included.▪ The products priced per endpoint, device or user: next-generation antivirus and Falcon Insight EDR/XDR, Falcon Complete Next-Gen MDR and OverWatch managed hunting, Counter Adversary Operations threat intelligence, Exposure Management, Falcon for IT, Data Protection, Charlotte AI, AIDR (from the Pangea acquisition of September 2025) and Seraphic browser security (February 2026).

What sets price. Published self-service list prices are $59.99 per device-year for Falcon Go (capped at 100 devices), $99.99 for Pro and $184.99 for Enterprise; Falcon Complete is quote-only (crowdstrike.com/en-us/pricing, accessed 2026-09-02) [web]. Falcon for IT launched at $20 per endpoint-year and Charlotte AI at $20 per endpoint-year with a query allocation and paid query packs, the only two per-module list prices published anywhere [deck: Fal.Con 2023 2023-09-20, slide 40]. Realized price is below list, and management publishes no series: "Our ASPs remain consistent" (Q4 FY2023 call) and "We've never been a company that has increased our prices to get more ARR" (Q4 FY2024 call, CFO). Discounts scale with commitment ("The more they commit, the bigger the discounts", Q1 FY2026 call). The median CrowdStrike buyer in a procurement-benchmark sample paid $55,300 a year across 623 purchases with an average negotiated saving of 14.2% (vendr.com/marketplace/crowdstrike, page dated February 2026, accessed 2026-09-02) [web]. Three forces have lowered the blended realized price while enterprise list prices held: Falcon Go at the bottom of the range, MSSP wholesale at an implied $16-30 per endpoint-year on the Kroll anchor, and the FY2025-FY2026 commitment packages.

What drives volume. The FY2026 10-K names three drivers: "the number of subscription customers, the number of endpoints per customer, and the number of cloud modules included in the subscription". None of the three is published as a unit count; the customer count was last given at 29,000 for January 31, 2024.

What drives cost. Subscription cost of revenue was $1,016m in FY2026, 22.3% of subscription revenue. The FY2026 increase of $181m decomposes into cloud hosting +$46.4m, employee-related +$43.1m on 16% higher average headcount, data-centre depreciation +$33.4m, internal-use software amortisation +$24.9m, stock compensation +$18.1m and allocated overhead +$16.8m (FY2026 10-K, Cost of Revenue). Hosting and depreciation, the volume-driven items, were 44% of the increase.▪

1.2 Emerging platform solutions: Cloud Security, Next-Gen Identity, Next-Gen SIEM

About 37% of ending ARR at July 2026 and about 32% of revenue. Three lines with three pricing units, sold onto the same sensor through the same channel.▪ The Q2 FY2027 10-Q widened the disclosed pricing units to "per-endpoint, per-identity, per-cloud sensor, per-user, per-device, and per-gigabyte of daily ingestion", against the FY2026 10-K's "per-endpoint and per-module".

Falcon Cloud Security protects cloud workloads: runtime detection and blocking through the same sensor on Linux hosts, container nodes and Kubernetes, plus agentless posture scanning layered on top. Committed list pricing runs $34-114 per workload-year across volume tiers, with platform commitments 22-34% below list (softwarecontractnegotiation.com, article dated 2026-05-26, accessed 2026-09-02) [web]; AWS Marketplace pay-as-you-go is $0.023 per host-hour, or $201 per host-year (aws.amazon.com listing prodview-vubjuepxztndi, accessed 2026-09-02) [web]. The two channels differ by 2-6x, and the negotiation source says the contractual definition of a workload alone moves the billed count by 30-60%.

Next-Gen Identity watches authentication traffic on domain controllers through the sensor already installed there, and adds SaaS posture (Falcon Shield, from Adaptive Shield), privileged access launched in FY2026, and continuous authorization (SGNL, February 2026). Adding identity to an endpoint subscription was described as "a sizable uplift to ASP, which can be north of 30%" (Q2 FY2023 call, Quartr).

Next-Gen SIEM bills per gigabyte per day of third-party data ingested. CrowdStrike-generated telemetry is not charged and every Falcon Insight customer gets 10 GB/day of third-party ingestion free▪: "we actually don't charge customers for data that CrowdStrike generates... They only pay for the ingest of the third-party data" (Q2 FY2026 call). The per-gigabyte rate is the highest among the scaled vendors. CrowdStrike's third-party ingest lists at roughly $2,170-2,680 per GB/day-year (AWS pay-as-you-go at $0.00595 per MB with 13-month retention; UK G-Cloud 14 at £2,000 per GB/day-year, realm.security, accessed 2026-09-02) [web] against roughly $1,000 for Splunk Cloud at a 50 GB/day deployment and $750-1,570 for Microsoft Sentinel from commitment tiers to pay-as-you-go (siemcostcalculator.com, accessed 2026-09-02) [web]. The saving comes from the billing base, and its size depends on the customer's data mix. The CFO's figure is that "80% of our SIEM, the security comes from us, comes from Falcon... And then you've got 20% from a third party. So we've made it really attractive on pricing for the first party, like sometimes it's free" (Morgan Stanley fireside, 2026-03-05). On that mix a customer bills a fifth of its volume at roughly twice the incumbent rate and pays about 40% of a Splunk bill [estimate: 0.20 multiplied by a 2.0x rate ratio, using the CFO's 80/20 mix and the rate cards above; management publishes no customer-level comparison, and a customer whose logs are mostly firewall, cloud-provider and application data saves much less]. Microsoft applies the same structure in reverse, ingesting its own Microsoft 365 and Defender logs free.

1.3 Falcon Flex

Flex is the commercial model that now applies to both franchises and the reason ARR and contract value have separated. A customer commits a dollar pool for one to five years at a pre-negotiated rate card across every module, draws it down as it activates modules, endpoints or workloads, trials modules in-app, and "re-Flexes" by adding to the pool.▪ Revenue recognition, ARR treatment and cash terms match ordinary subscriptions (Fal.Con 2024 briefing). From FY2027 every deal is Flex unless management grants an exception (Morgan Stanley fireside, 2026-03-05).

A Fortune 500 technology conglomerate went from $5m of ARR on seven modules ($14m of contract value over about three years) to $24m on ten modules ($103m over five years) to $57m on fourteen modules ($246m over four years) [deck: Fal.Con 2025 2025-09-17, slide 50]. Contract value moved 17.6x while ARR moved 11.4x, because the term lengthened and then shortened. "Ending ARR of Flex-adopted accounts" is the whole account's ARR, including the endpoint base the customer already had, so it is a mix measure. And the 10-K states the other side of the commitment: "if our customers are not able to fully utilize their product subscriptions (including in connection with our flexible subscription offering), we may experience increased contraction" (FY2026 10-K, Key Metrics). Utilisation was last disclosed at above 75%, at Q2 FY2026 [deck: Fal.Con 2025 2025-09-17, slide 49].

1.5 The endpoint count, from three angles

Three constructions of the protected-endpoint base at January 2026 overlap at 20-40m [estimate: the three angles that follow]. Angle A divides endpoint-bundle ARR of $2.0-2.35bn (60-70% of the $3.35bn core residual) by a realized bundle price of $65-140, giving 14-36m. Angle B uses disclosed deal anchors: a US government agency land across more than 200,000 hosts at an eight-figure value (Q1 FY2027 call) and Kroll's 450,000 endpoints at an "almost eight-figure" value (Q3 FY2026 call), applied across the direct and MSSP mix, giving 22-45m. Angle C works from market share: 17.7% of the IDC modern-endpoint category implies a market of about $12bn in calendar 2022 if IDC counted nearly all of CrowdStrike's subscription revenue, against the $6.3-8.3bn that the 65-85% endpoint-counted share in §4.6 produces. At a market blended price of $30-60 per endpoint-year the larger figure covers 200-400m endpoints, of which CrowdStrike's own endpoint revenue at $75-165 per endpoint-year buys 15-25m.

The direct-enterprise and MSSP price anchors differ by 3-5x. One tenth of endpoints sold through MSSPs at wholesale lowers the blended realized price by 8-10% with no change in enterprise pricing. The MSSP business went from "a sub-$100 million MSSP business to more than $1.3 billion" in just over three years (Q4 FY2026 call), roughly a quarter of ending ARR, and an MSSP counts as one customer in the dollar-based net retention rate and in the module-adoption percentages.

2. Key technologies and technical differentiators

Three parts of the platform are hard to copy and a longer list is not.

The Falcon sensor. One agent per endpoint or workload, combining a Windows kernel driver with user-mode modules and supporting macOS and Linux. It keeps a local graph of the machine, runs machine-learning and behavioural detection on the device, blocks locally, keeps protecting when offline, and installs without a reboot. It streams only what detection needs: the IPO prospectus put an unfiltered endpoint at about 100 GB of system events a day, so a 100,000-endpoint enterprise would generate more than a petabyte daily after compression (424B4, "High Fidelity Data and Smart Filtering"). Kurtz gives four reasons the kernel is needed: telemetry visibility, the ability to block, anti-tamper protection and performance (Goldman conference, 2024-09-11). What makes the sensor hard to copy is fourteen years of Windows-kernel engineering against an operating system whose interfaces change, plus the install base that makes the collected data useful.▪ What makes it fragile is the same code path: on July 19, 2024 a content configuration update crashed Windows systems worldwide because a template with 21 input fields met sensor code expecting 20, a content validator with a logic error passed it, and the content interpreter performed no runtime bounds check (CrowdStrike root-cause analysis, accessed 2026-09-02) [web].

Outside evidence for the sensor's efficacy comes from third-party evaluations and from retention. Gartner placed CrowdStrike highest for ability to execute and furthest for completeness of vision in the 2026 Magic Quadrant for Endpoint Protection Platforms, the fourth consecutive year in that position and the seventh consecutive time as a Leader; Microsoft and SentinelOne are also Leaders. In MITRE's 2025 ATT&CK Enterprise round, the first to span identity, endpoint and cloud, CrowdStrike reported 100% detection and 100% protection with no false positives (crowdstrike.com press release, 2025-12-10, accessed 2026-09-02) [web]. Gross retention has been 97-98% in every year since FY2020, and endpoint ARR growth accelerated for four consecutive quarters to Q2 FY2027.

The substitution threat is Microsoft, in two forms. Defender for Endpoint ships inside the Microsoft 365 E5 licence, so its marginal price to an E5 tenant is close to zero. And in June 2025 Microsoft announced a Windows endpoint security platform under which "security products like anti-virus and endpoint protection solutions can run in user mode just as apps do", with a private preview from July 2025 for eight vendors including CrowdStrike, SentinelOne, Sophos, Trellix and Trend Micro (securityweek.com, 2025-06-27, accessed 2026-09-02) [web]. Microsoft's November 2025 statement adds that "We will continue to support third-party kernel mode drivers" and gives no general-availability date (blogs.windows.com, accessed 2026-09-02) [web]. A user-mode platform would lower the crash blast radius for every vendor, and it would also lower the kernel-engineering barrier that has protected the incumbents.▪ CrowdStrike's president at Fal.Con 2024: "there is no post-kernel architecture... The kernel today has 2,000-plus drivers." The leading indicator is a Microsoft announcement that in-box kernel interfaces replace third-party drivers for enforcement.

Threat Graph and the labelled corpus. A proprietary graph database links process, file, network and user events across every sensor, enriches them with intelligence, and recognises attack chains whose individual steps look benign. Scale is stated on shifting bases: more than 1 trillion endpoint events per week at the IPO, "more than 1 trillion security events per day across approximately 2 trillion vertices, analyzing 15-plus petabytes of data" at Q4 FY2026. The graph itself can be rebuilt. What a competitor would also need is the labelling: Falcon Complete, OverWatch and the incident-response team produced more than 15 million labelled annotations and more than 800 incident-response engagements in the twelve months to September 2025▪ [deck: Fal.Con 2025 2025-09-17, slides 37-38], which requires running the managed-detection and incident-response businesses as a by-product. Kurtz calls it "cyber reinforced learning from human feedback... at scale" and the FY2026 10-K adopted the phrase. The observable consequence is Charlotte AI Detection Triage, benchmarked at more than 98% agreement with Falcon Complete analyst decisions (crowdstrike.com/en-us/platform/charlotte-ai, accessed 2026-09-02) [web], a vendor-reported figure.

First-party data gravity in Next-Gen SIEM. LogScale, bought as Humio in March 2021, is an index-free log store: data is compressed and written without index builds, so ingestion has no lag and queries scan compressed blocks. CrowdStrike's published benchmark is more than one petabyte of ingestion a day on 45 nodes of 96 cores, 30m events a second, with sub-second search. The store can be rebuilt; the data cannot. Every Falcon customer's endpoint, identity and cloud telemetry is already in the platform, so a SIEM migration starts with roughly 80% of the volume in place and the customer pays only for the rest.▪ Palo Alto's XSIAM shows the same construct can be built from a firewall-plus-endpoint footprint: it reached more than $700m of ARR growing 70% with about 1,000 customers in FY2026 (PANW Q4 FY2026 call, 2026-09-01) [web], level with CrowdStrike's more than $695m.▪

Falcon Flex is a contract structure. Kurtz: "we've seen others copy it to the point where they can't even change the name Flex" (Fal.Con 2025). It differentiates only in combination with 33 modules on one agent and in-app trials.

AIDR, from the September 2025 Pangea acquisition, maps users, prompts, models, agents and MCP servers, detects prompt injection and data leakage, and enforces policy, delivered through the existing sensor and a browser extension. It is priced on token allowances with paid top-up packs, consumable through Flex (Q2 FY2027 call). Its claimed advantage is position: "Agents run on the endpoint. They make tool calls, access files, invoke APIs and move data at the process level" (Q1 FY2027 call), which is the endpoint franchise restated. Its ARR has been reported only as multiples, more than 5x sequentially at Q4 FY2026, more than 250% at Q1 FY2027 and "nearly tripled versus Q1" at Q2 FY2027, and never as a dollar level. Kurtz's sizing, "I think the AIDR business can be bigger than the EDR business", is unquantified.

Shipping speed bears on the FY2031-FY2036 targets. Product announcements at Fal.Con have reached general availability in about three to nine months: Falcon Flex announced September 2023 with first deals cited March 2024; Charlotte AI beta December 2023, generally available March 2024; Falcon for IT September 2023 to March 2024; just-in-time privileged access September 2024 to Q1 FY2026. The exceptions are platform rewrites and acquisitions. Project Kestrel, the new console announced September 2024, was shown as a release candidate in September 2025 and described by the president as "a multiyear project that we have started". FalconID phish-proof multi-factor authentication and risk-based patching, both announced at Fal.Con 2025, were not cited as shipped on any call through August 2026.

Infrastructure is the dependency growing fastest. The platform is hosted on "a mix of third-party data centers, primarily Amazon Web Services... and our data centers, hosted in colocation facilities", and the 10-K states that "any renegotiation or renewal of our agreement with AWS may be on terms that are significantly less favorable to us". Data-centre equipment purchased but not yet placed in service was $273.7m at July 31, 2026, up from $161.9m six months earlier, and purchases of property and equipment were $124.4m in Q2 FY2027 against $30.5m a year earlier.

3. Competitive advantages and moat assessment

3.1 Core Falcon platform

CrowdStrike's endpoint franchise earns high cash returns on a balance sheet funded by customer prepayments, and its installed base has survived two well-funded attempts to break it.▪ The first is Microsoft's bundling of Defender for Endpoint into the Microsoft 365 E5 licence, running since about 2019; through it, ending ARR grew from $600m at January 31, 2020 to $5,841m at July 31, 2026. The second was the company's own outage: gross retention was "over 97%, down less than 0.5 percentage point" in the quarter after July 19, 2024 and finished FY2025 at 97% against 98% a year earlier, while net retention declined from 119% to 112% and recovered to 115% in FY2026. The mechanism is a sensor on every device a customer owns, a telemetry and label corpus a competitor cannot buy, a 24/7 human detection layer that also produces the training labels, and a module cross-sell that raises the cost of leaving with every module added: 51% of subscription customers use six or more modules at Q2 FY2027, up from 24% at FY2021.▪

The advantage is real and defensible for now, and three facts limit it. Efficacy has not converted into price. The pitch is total cost of ownership ("better outcomes at a cheaper cost", Q2 FY2027 call), Next-Gen SIEM is sold as "very disruptive from a price point" (Q2 FY2027 call), Flex discounts scale with commitment, and the post-outage packages added discounts and extended terms worth about $80m of ARR value. There is no margin premium over the closest platform peer: GAAP operating margin was (6.1)% in FY2026 against Palo Alto Networks' 13.5% in FY2025▪, and on the non-GAAP basis both companies use, CrowdStrike's 21.7% for FY2026 trails Palo Alto's 29.2% for FY2026 (PR Newswire, 2026-09-01, accessed 2026-09-02) [web]. And cash conversion declined for five years: free cash flow went from 34.7% of revenue in FY2021 to 27.2% in FY2026 on operating cash flow less purchases of property and equipment, the peer-comparable basis used in the tables below, and from 33.5% to 25.7% on the company's own definition, which also deducts capitalised internal-use software; free cash flow after stock compensation went from 17.6% to 4.4% of revenue on the first basis.▪

Microsoft is the reason this advantage does not support pricing power or throw off excess returns with little reinvestment to defend it. IDC ranks Microsoft first in modern endpoint security by revenue share for CY2023 (25.8%) and CY2024 (28.6%, growing 28.2%), which Microsoft describes as a third consecutive year at number one (Microsoft Security Blog, 2025-08-27, accessed 2026-09-02) [web]; CrowdStrike's last self-published IDC share is 17.7% for the year to June 2022, when it ranked first (Q4 FY2023 call). Both vendors displace legacy antivirus, which both CEOs put at about half the market, so both leaders have so far gained mostly from the same donor pool. Microsoft also supplies the Windows kernel interfaces the sensor depends on and sets a reference price inside a bundle CrowdStrike does not sell. CrowdStrike spent 28.8% of revenue on R&D and 38.1% on sales and marketing in FY2026 to hold the position.

Management claims. The FY2026 10-K makes four: a data network effect ("The more data that is fed into our Falcon platform, the more intelligent the AI Security Cloud becomes... creating a powerful network effect"), single-sensor architecture ("we do not believe any of our competitors currently have a true platform offering equivalent to the Falcon platform"), human expertise as training data, and lower total cost of ownership through consolidation. Its own qualifiers are in the same document: competitors "enjoy greater resources, recognition, deeper customer relationships, larger existing customer bases, or more mature intellectual property portfolios", larger competitors "may offer lower pricing than we do", and on patents, "the skills and ingenuity of our employees and the functionality and frequent enhancements to our solutions are larger contributors to our success in the marketplace".

External sources. Gartner corroborates efficacy. A customer test came from Gap's CISO, speaking at CrowdStrike's own investor event: "We're also an E5 shop. So we looked at replacing CrowdStrike with Microsoft. Commercially, looked like it made sense... switching to a Microsoft solution, even if you discount all of like the switching costs and the pain to migrate, ended up costing us more because there are variable costs that's hard to predict in the Microsoft world", and on efficacy, "CrowdStrike was able to detect and block the EDR bypass technique and completely frank, Defender for endpoint did not" (Fal.Con 2025). Management's version of the same arithmetic is that for an enterprise above 50,000 employees, upgrading from E3 to E5 "would be at least $2.3 million more than their CrowdStrike subscription... this would grow to $4.7 million by year 5" (Q1 FY2024 call). Against that, IDC's revenue-share measure puts Microsoft first, and Microsoft's security business passed $20bn of annual revenue in January 2023 (cybersecuritydive.com, accessed 2026-09-02) [web] against CrowdStrike's $5.84bn of ARR.

Ground-up view. A competitive endpoint product needs a kernel-certified sensor on three operating systems, a cloud that ingests and correlates the telemetry, a 24/7 hunting organisation, and a labelled corpus of adversary behaviour. CrowdStrike spent $1,385m on R&D and $1,831m on sales and marketing in FY2026. SentinelOne, the only scaled pure-play challenger, spent 32.3% of a $1,001m revenue base on R&D and reported a $(321.3)m GAAP loss from operations. No pure-play entrant has reached scale since SentinelOne; entry now comes from platforms that already own an endpoint footprint. Switching costs are the strongest element: replacing the sensor means touching every device, and Kroll's migration of 450,000 endpoints off a competing next-gen product took three quarters to reach a majority. Scale shows up as about one point of non-GAAP subscription margin a year and no movement in the GAAP figure, which is a modest cost advantage. The claimed network effect is a learning effect on pooled telemetry, one-sided, and its test is whether share and engagement compound with the installed base: engagement does, and share against Microsoft does not on the available measure.

Return on invested capital. Conventional ROIC cannot be computed. On the standard definition, equity plus debt plus lease liabilities less cash and investments, invested capital has been negative in every year of the company's history, from $(419)m at January 2018 to $(14)m at January 2026, because deferred revenue and accrued liabilities exceed operating assets. Customers fund the working capital and then some, and stock compensation pays for about a fifth of the cost base. GAAP NOPAT is negative in every year, so the GAAP ratio is undefined. Adding deferred revenue back and treating it as customer financing gives an operating asset base the company actually built:

ROIC basis: non-GAAP operating income x (1 − 21%), divided by the average of opening and closing invested capital before deferred-revenue funding, where invested capital = equity + long-term debt + operating lease liabilities − cash − short-term investments − strategic investments + total deferred revenue.

FY2021 FY2022 FY2023 FY2024 FY2025 FY2026
Invested capital before deferred revenue ($m) 642 1,321 1,874 2,653 3,441 4,739
Non-GAAP NOPAT ($m) 49 155 281 522 695 827
ROIC 9.5% 15.8% 17.6% 23.0% 22.8% 20.2%
ROIIC, three-year rolling 15.8% 14.4% 22.6% 23.5% 25.5% 19.0%

ROIC peaked at 23.0% in FY2024 and has declined 2.8 points since, because invested capital before deferred revenue grew 79% over two years while non-GAAP NOPAT grew 59%, and $747m of the $2,086m increase is goodwill and intangibles from Adaptive Shield, Onum, Pangea and the FY2026 deals.▪ The FY2026 non-GAAP return of 20.2% is against an assumed 9-10% cost of capital for an equity-funded software business; the GAAP return is negative.

CrowdStrike converted growth into non-GAAP margin (7.1% to 21.7%) while GAAP margin went into stock compensation and cash margin went into data-centre capex and incident costs. On every GAAP and cash measure the gap to the profitable peers widened against CrowdStrike over five years; Palo Alto, Zscaler, Fortinet and Okta each reduced stock-compensation intensity while CrowdStrike raised it. The FY2027 re-acceleration is the first reversal of the growth-gap trend since FY2021 and is the strongest current evidence for the moat; the margin and cash trends have not yet reversed on a GAAP basis.

Business-model analogues. Datadog is the closest match: a single agent installed fleet-wide, telemetry pooled in the vendor's cloud, modules cross-sold on that agent, and multi-product adoption as the disclosed KPI (55% of customers on four or more products and 33% on six or more at December 31, 2025, Datadog FY2025 10-K), with the same exposure to a platform owner's native tools. It breaks as an analogue because monitoring does not hold a security control's 97% gross retention. ServiceNow matches the land-and-expand shape of one platform sold as successive workflows, with a 98% renewal rate in each of 2023-2025, and breaks because no supplier of ServiceNow's runtime is also its largest competitor. Verisk matches the pooled-contributory-data claim and breaks because Verisk's contributors cannot rebuild the dataset, whereas Microsoft observes every Windows endpoint without a third-party sensor. Of the three, the evidence supports a moat of Datadog's strength.▪

3.2 Emerging platform solutions

The three emerging lines inherit the endpoint franchise's advantage and add little of their own. Each is a module switched on for a sensor the customer already runs, and combined ending ARR rose from more than $850m at January 2024 to more than $2.18bn at July 2026, 2.6x in two and a half years.▪ The trio grew above 39% in the year to July 2026 against Okta at +10.6% and Elastic at +15.1% in their latest quarters and CyberArk at +18.5% in the December 2025 quarter, its last before Palo Alto acquired it, which is what taking share looks like.

The advantage is defensible for now and open to erosion, and it is weaker than the endpoint franchise's on three counts. In none of the three lines does CrowdStrike hold the position it holds on the endpoint.▪ In cloud, Wiz passed $1bn of ARR before Google closed its $32bn purchase on March 11, 2026, against Falcon Cloud Security's more than $905m; Wiz's latest-year growth is 43% on the source's own dated points ($700m in 2025 to above $1bn at close) and 59-74% annualising from $500m at end-2024, against CrowdStrike's above 29% (valueaddvc.com, accessed 2026-09-02) [web]. In SIEM, Gartner placed CrowdStrike in the Visionaries quadrant of the 2025 Magic Quadrant, below the Leaders on ability to execute (crowdstrike.com press release, 2025-10-09, accessed 2026-09-02) [web], while IDC named it a Leader in its June 2026 MarketScape, citing that "Many of the data feeds traditionally routed into a SIEM, including endpoint, identity, and cloud signals, originate inside the Falcon platform itself" (crowdstrike.com press release, 2026-06-23, accessed 2026-09-02) [web]; Palo Alto's XSIAM reached the same ARR scale with a faster growth rate. In identity, the FY2026-FY2027 re-acceleration came from an acquired product (Falcon Shield, +185% at Q2 FY2027) and a privileged-access product launched from zero (+35x), while Microsoft owns the identity store the sensor must be granted access to and CyberArk, with $1.44bn of ARR, is now inside Palo Alto.

Second, there is no pricing power in the segment. Management calls Next-Gen SIEM "very disruptive from a price point" and sells cloud security as "the right outcome at a much lower cost than the competitors" (Q4 FY2026 call). The SIEM saving is structural to any endpoint vendor and is available to Microsoft and Palo Alto on the same terms; Splunk and Elastic cannot copy it. Third, no cost advantage has appeared: GAAP subscription gross margin was 77.7-78.0% in each of FY2024, FY2025 and FY2026 while the trio rose from 25% to 36% of ARR, and the "collect once, monetize many times" claim is a FY2029 target (82-85% non-GAAP subscription gross margin), not a reported result.▪

The attack that has been tried and not repelled is Wiz's agentless posture model, which took the posture layer from 2021 onward. Kurtz's own description: CSPM "was an easy button for a lot of customers. And certainly, vendors had success in that area" (Q2 FY2026 call). CrowdStrike kept the runtime layer, reports "multiple Wiz replacements" (Q3 FY2026 call) and is a Frost Radar leader in cloud workload protection for the fourth consecutive time, and now sells both layers. Both vendors roughly doubled over two years, Wiz from $500m to above $1bn and CrowdStrike's cloud line from above $400m (January 2024) to above $800m (January 2026). Two scaled vendors with the larger one growing at least as fast, and a hyperscaler owning the larger one, is a contested duopoly.▪

The same two analogues apply. Datadog matches again, for the agent-plus-modules shape and the gigabyte-priced log line. Palo Alto Networks is the direct mirror: data gravity from an installed footprint extended into SIEM, cloud and identity, with the same platform contracting; it is stronger on margins (29% non-GAAP operating margin in FY2026) and weaker on organic breadth, since its identity and cloud lines were bought. Microsoft's E5 security attach is the stronger form of the same construct, because the bundle owner also owns the identity store and the operating system, which is why it is a competitor and not a peer-strength analogue.

The company reports one segment and no line-level margin, so the returns comparison above covers both franchises.

4.1 Endpoint security

CrowdStrike stopped citing an IDC share after the Q4 FY2023 call in March 2023 and now cites Gartner Magic Quadrant placement and an "endpoint security ISV" share, a category that excludes Microsoft.▪ Canalys ranked CrowdStrike first "ahead of Microsoft" in research cited on the Q3 FY2024 call, so the two research houses disagreed on the CY2023 leader.

Estimated CY2024 shares, built from CrowdStrike's mid-2022 endpoint revenue grown forward: a market of $10-14bn, Microsoft 28.6% on $3-4bn of revenue, CrowdStrike roughly 12-20% and rank 2 on $1.6-2.1bn of endpoint-module revenue, SentinelOne 5-7% on about $0.7bn [estimate: arithmetic in §4.6]. IDC's allocation of Microsoft 365 E5 bundle revenue to Defender is IDC's method and is not public, so Microsoft's share is only as reliable as that allocation.

Concentration rose but the category is still not concentrated. In the mid-2022 window the top ten vendors held about 72% of the category and the HHI on the disclosed shares was about 760-860 depending on how the legacy block outside Microsoft is split. Rolling forward to CY2024 with Microsoft at 28.6% and CrowdStrike at 12-20% gives about 1,300-1,650 [estimate: HHI on disclosed shares with the legacy block split six ways]. On the 2010 Horizontal Merger Guidelines the top of that range crosses into moderate concentration and the bottom does not. Microsoft's gain accounts for the whole move.

Microsoft sets the reference price. Defender for Endpoint ships inside Microsoft 365 E5, and from mid-2026 inside the E7 suite, which "brings together Copilot, E5, Entra, and Agent 365... Just 2 months after launch, hundreds of enterprise customers have already purchased millions of seats", with EY at 400,000 seats (Microsoft Q4 FY2026 call, 2026-07-29) [web]. CrowdStrike answers on total cost of ownership and says it wins "8 out of 10 times when an enterprise customer tests" (April 2023 briefing; repeated Q1 FY2024 call), a figure it has since described as "rising" without giving a number.

The legacy pool has not moved on management's own account: 48% of the market on legacy antivirus in September 2023, 50% in December 2025, "about half" in August 2026, and SentinelOne's CEO says "nearly half of the sector still relies on legacy antivirus" (fool.com transcript, 2026-08-31, accessed 2026-09-02) [web]. Three years of continuous displacement by two vendors have not changed the stated figure, so either the estimate is loosely maintained or new endpoints land on legacy tools as fast as old ones leave.▪

CrowdStrike is about 4.8x SentinelOne on company ARR at July 2026 and about 4x on the endpoint line [estimate: core residual against SentinelOne's endpoint-weighted ARR], and it added $1,011m of ARR in FY2026 against SentinelOne's $199m. Its single-quarter net new ARR of $333m in Q2 FY2027 exceeded SentinelOne's net new ARR for all of FY2026.▪ Against Microsoft it trails by roughly 9-17 share points on IDC's count [estimate: 28.6% against a 12-20% CrowdStrike range, §4.6]. The displacement units disclosed on the calls: Carbon Black "an exodus of nearly 0.5 million" endpoints, Kroll 450,000 off a competing next-gen product, a US agency across more than 200,000 hosts, a financial-services firm with "hundreds of thousands of endpoints", and a European automaker replacing a next-gen EDR, a legacy SIEM and a vulnerability product in one eight-figure Flex.

4.2 Managed detection and response

CrowdStrike ranked first by MDR revenue in Gartner's managed-security-services market-share reports for the 2021 and 2022 data years, the latest ranking it has published, and says "Of the top 25 MDR vendors by market share defined by Gartner, 88% have built their MDR services on top of the Falcon platform" (Q1 FY2024 call). The market is consolidating around firms that do not own an endpoint agent, and so far the acquirers have moved their estates onto Falcon: Sophos bought Secureworks for about $859m; Zscaler bought Red Canary, which then migrated its endpoint customers to Falcon "through a multimillion-dollar Q2 transaction" (Q2 FY2026 call); Kroll migrated 450,000 endpoints and then signed a multiyear Flex growing its spend more than 3x (Q2 FY2027 call). Huntress, the SMB and MSP vendor, passed $250m of ARR growing 65% across 270,000 businesses (huntress.com press release, 2026-07-30, accessed 2026-09-02) [web]. Arctic Wolf is private; Sacra estimates $438m of ARR for 2023 [web], an estimate.

4.3 Exposure management

CrowdStrike's line passed $300m of ARR at Q2 FY2026, from "line of sight to $300 million" two quarters earlier, and accelerated sequentially in Q2 FY2027. That is a third to a half of any one incumbent: Tenable revenue $999m in CY2025 (+11%), Rapid7 $860m (+2%) with ARR of $840m flat and 2026 revenue guided down 2-3%, Qualys $669m (+10%). The three together grew about 8% on $2.5bn of revenue. In July 2026 CrowdStrike agreed to buy XM Cyber's technology assets for $145.0m in cash and shares plus further shares to be set at closing, with no ARR or revenue attached; Schwarz Group had bought XM Cyber for $700m in 2021 (calcalistech.com, 2026-07-17, accessed 2026-09-02) [web].

4.4 Cloud, identity and SIEM

CrowdStrike is not the scale leader in any of the three.▪ The observable vendor figures at their latest disclosed dates:
